relationships.subject: spinal cord endothelial VEGFR2 knockout
relationships.evidence_quote: VEGFR2scECKO mice demonstrated an increase in expression of hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF1α) and glucose transporter 3 (GLUT3, supplemental Figure 5A and B, available at http://links.lww.com/PAIN/B597) in dorsal horn neurons

relationships.subject: DMOG
relationships.evidence_quote: CA7 expression was increased in the spinal cord neurons as was GLUT3 and HIF1α.

relationships.subject: acetazolamide
relationships.evidence_quote: The nonselective carbonic anhydrase inhibitor ACZ delivered by intraperitoneal injection attenuated DMOG-induced nociceptive behavioural hypersensitivity.

relationships.subject: hypoxia
relationships.evidence_quote: In addition, KCC2 was downregulated (supplemental Figure 6C, available at http://links.lww.com/PAIN/B597).

relationships.subject: VEGF-A165
relationships.evidence_quote: VEGF-A165 increased solute permeability of the blood–spinal cord barrier when compared with vehicle control (Figs. 2F and G) which was blocked by treatment with VEGFR2 inhibitor ZM323881 (Figs. 2F and G).

relationships.subject: hypoxia
relationships.evidence_quote: In addition, there was an increased number of dorsal horn neurons expressing fos immunoreactivity after intrathecal DMOG injection (Figs. 6C and D).

key_findings: Spinal cord endothelial VEGFR2 knockout causes vascular rarefaction, dorsal horn neuron hypoxia (HIF1α, GLUT3, CA7 up) and heat hypersensitivity.
The hypoxia mimetic DMOG induced hypersensitivity and neuronal activation, attenuated by the carbonic anhydrase inhibitor acetazolamide.
